reception.title: Early years foundation stage statutory framework (group and school-based providers)

nursery.title: Development Matters: non-statutory curriculum guidance for the EYFS

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Enjoy listening to longer stories and can remember much of what happens

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Pay attention to more than one thing at a time, which can be difficult

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Use a wider range of vocabulary

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Understand a question or instruction that has 2 parts, such as: "Get your coat and wait at the door"

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Understand 'why' questions, like: "Why do you think the caterpillar got so fat?"

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Sing a large repertoire of songs

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Know many rhymes, be able to talk about familiar books, and be able to tell a long story

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Develop their communication but may continue to have problems with irregular tenses and plurals, such as 'runned' for 'ran', 'swimmed' for 'swam'

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Develop their pronunciation but may have problems saying: some sounds: r, j, th, ch, and sh

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Develop their pronunciation but may have problems saying: multi-syllabic words such as 'pterodactyl', 'planetarium' or 'hippopotamus'

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Use longer sentences of 4 to 6 words

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Be able to express a point of view and to debate when they disagree with an adult or a friend, using words as well as actions

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Start a conversation with an adult or a friend and continue it for many turns

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Use talk to organise themselves and their play: "Let's go on a bus… you sit there… I'll be the driver"

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Select and use activities and resources, with help when needed - this helps them to achieve a goal they have chosen or one which is suggested to them

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Develop their sense of responsibility and membership of a community

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Become more outgoing with unfamiliar people, in the safe context of their setting

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Show more confidence in new social situations

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Play with one or more other children, extending and elaborating play ideas

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Find solutions to conflicts and rivalries, for example, accepting that not everyone can be Spider-Man in the game, and suggesting other ideas

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Increasingly follow rules, understanding why they are important

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Remember rules without needing an adult to remind them

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Develop appropriate ways of being assertive

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Talk with others to solve conflicts

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Talk about their feelings using words like 'happy', 'sad', 'angry' or 'worried'

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Understand gradually how others might be feeling

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Be increasingly independent in meeting their own care needs, for example, brushing teeth, using the toilet, washing and drying their hands thoroughly

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Make healthy choices about food, drink, activity and toothbrushing

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Continue to develop their movement, balancing, riding (scooters, trikes and bikes) and ball skills

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Go up steps and stairs, or climb up apparatus, using alternate feet

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Skip, hop, stand on one leg and hold a pose for a game like musical statues

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Use large-muscle movements to wave flags and streamers, paint and make marks

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Start taking part in some group activities which they make up for themselves, or in teams

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Increasingly be able to use and remember sequences and patterns of movements which are related to music and rhythm

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Match their developing physical skills to tasks and activities in the setting, for example, they decide whether to crawl, walk or run across a plank, depending on its length and width

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Choose the right resources to carry out their own plan, for example, choosing a spade to enlarge a small hole they dug with a trowel

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Collaborate with others to manage large items, such as moving a long plank safely, carrying large hollow blocks

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Use one-handed tools and equipment, for example, making snips in paper with scissors

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Use a comfortable grip with good control when holding pens and pencils

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Show a preference for a dominant hand

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Be increasingly independent as they get dressed and undressed, for example, putting coats on and doing up zips

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Develop their phonological awareness, so that they can: spot and suggest rhymes

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Develop their phonological awareness, so that they can: count or clap syllables in a word

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Develop their phonological awareness, so that they can: recognise words with the same initial sound, such as money and mother

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Engage in extended conversations about stories, learning new vocabulary

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Use some of their print and letter knowledge in their early writing, for example, writing a pretend shopping list that starts at the top of the page, writing 'm' for mummy

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Write some or all of their name

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Write some letters accurately

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Develop fast recognition of up to 3 objects, without having to count them individually ('subitising')

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Recite numbers past 5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Say one number for each item in order: 1,2,3,4,5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Know that the last number reached when counting a small set of objects tells you how many there are in total ('cardinal principle')

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Show 'finger numbers' up to 5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Link numerals and amounts: for example, showing the right number of objects to match the numeral, up to 5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Experiment with their own symbols and marks as well as numerals

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Solve real-world mathematical problems with numbers up to 5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Compare quantities using language 'more than' and 'fewer than'

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and explore 2D and 3D shapes (for example, circles, rectangles, triangles and cuboids) using informal and mathematical language such as: sides

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and explore 2D and 3D shapes (for example, circles, rectangles, triangles and cuboids) using informal and mathematical language such as: corners

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and explore 2D and 3D shapes (for example, circles, rectangles, triangles and cuboids) using informal and mathematical language such as: straight

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and explore 2D and 3D shapes (for example, circles, rectangles, triangles and cuboids) using informal and mathematical language such as: flat

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and explore 2D and 3D shapes (for example, circles, rectangles, triangles and cuboids) using informal and mathematical language such as: round

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Understand position through words alone, for example, "The bag is under the table," with no pointing

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Describe a familiar route

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Discuss routes and locations, using words like 'in front of' and 'behind'

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Make comparisons between objects relating to size, length, weight and capacity

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Select shapes appropriately such as flat surfaces for building or a triangular prism for a roof

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Combine shapes to make new ones, for example, an arch or a bigger triangle

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Talk about and identify the patterns around them, for example, stripes on clothes or designs on rugs and wallpaper

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Use informal language like 'pointy', 'spotty' or 'blobs'

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Extend and create ABAB patterns - stick, leaf, stick, leaf

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Notice and correct an error in a repeating pattern

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Begin to describe a sequence of events, real or fictional, using words such as 'first', 'then…'

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Use all their senses in hands-on exploration of natural materials

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Explore collections of materials with similar or different properties

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Talk about what they see, using a wide vocabulary

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Begin to make sense of their own life story and family's history

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Show interest in different occupations

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Explore how things work

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Plant seeds and care for growing plants

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Understand the key features of the life cycle of a plant and an animal

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Begin to understand the need to respect and care for the natural environment and all living things

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Explore and talk about different forces they can feel

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Talk about the differences between materials and changes they notice

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Continue developing positive attitudes about the differences between people

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Know that there are different countries in the world and talk about the differences they have experienced or seen in photos

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Take part in simple pretend play, using an object to represent something else even though they are not similar

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Begin to develop complex stories using small world equipment like animal sets, dolls and dolls houses

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Make imaginative and complex 'small worlds' with blocks and construction kits, such as a city with different buildings and a park

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Explore different materials freely, to develop their ideas about how to use them and what to make

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Develop their own ideas and then decide which materials to use to express them

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Join different materials and explore different textures

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Create closed shapes with continuous lines and begin to use these shapes to represent objects

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Draw with increasing complexity and detail, such as representing a face with a circle and including details

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Use drawing to represent ideas like movement or loud noises

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Show different emotions in their drawings and paintings, like happiness, sadness, fear

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Explore colour and colour mixing

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Show different emotions in their drawings - happiness, sadness, fear

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Listen with increased attention to sounds

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Respond to what they have heard, expressing their thoughts and feelings

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Remember and sing entire songs

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Sing the pitch of a tone sung by another person ('pitch match')

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Sing the melodic shape (moving melody, such as up and down, down and up) of familiar songs

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Create their own songs or improvise a song around one they know

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Play instruments with increasing control to express their feelings and ideas

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Listen attentively and respond to what they hear with relevant questions, comments and actions when being read to and during whole class discussions and small group interactions

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Make comments about what they have heard and ask questions to clarify their understanding

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Hold conversation when engaged in back-and-forth exchanges with their teacher and peers

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Participate in small group, class and one-to-one discussions, offering their own ideas, using recently introduced vocabulary

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Offer explanations for why things might happen, making use of recently introduced vocabulary from stories, non-fiction, rhymes and poems when appropriate

statements.subject: Communication and Language
statements.text: Express their ideas and feelings about their experiences using full sentences, including use of past, present and future tenses and making use of conjunctions, with modelling and support from their teacher

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Show an understanding of their own feelings and those of others and begin to regulate their behaviour accordingly

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Set and work towards simple goals, being able to wait for what they want and control their immediate impulses when appropriate

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Give focused attention to what the teacher says, responding appropriately even when engaged in activity, and show an ability to follow instructions involving several ideas or actions

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Be confident to try new activities and show independence, resilience and perseverance in the face of challenge

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Explain the reasons for rules, know right from wrong and try to behave accordingly

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Manage their own basic hygiene and personal needs, including dressing, going to the toilet and understanding the importance of healthy food choices

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Work and play cooperatively and take turns with others

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Form positive attachments to adults and friendships with peers

statements.subject: Personal, Social and Emotional Development
statements.text: Show sensitivity to their own and to others' needs

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Negotiate space and obstacles safely, with consideration for themselves and others

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Demonstrate strength, balance and coordination when playing

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Move energetically, such as running, jumping, dancing, hopping, skipping and climbing

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Hold a pencil effectively in preparation for fluent writing - using the tripod grip in almost all cases

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Use a range of small tools, including scissors, paint brushes and cutlery

statements.subject: Physical Development
statements.text: Begin to show accuracy and care when drawing

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Demonstrate understanding of what has been read to them by retelling stories and narratives using their own words and recently introduced vocabulary

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Anticipate - where appropriate - key events in stories

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Use and understand recently introduced vocabulary during discussions about stories, non-fiction, rhymes and poems and during role-play

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Say a sound for each letter in the alphabet and at least 10 digraphs

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Read words consistent with their phonic knowledge by sound-blending

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Read aloud simple sentences and books that are consistent with their phonic knowledge, including some common exception words

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Write recognisable letters, most of which are correctly formed

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Spell words by identifying sounds in them and representing the sounds with a letter or letters

statements.subject: Literacy
statements.text: Write simple phrases and sentences that can be read by others

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Have a deep understanding of numbers to 10, including the composition of each number

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Subitise (recognise quantities without counting) up to 5

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Automatically recall (without reference to rhymes, counting or other aids) number bonds up to 5 (including subtraction facts) and some number bonds to 10, including double facts

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Verbally count beyond 20, recognising the pattern of the counting system

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Compare quantities up to 10 in different contexts, recognising when one quantity is greater than, less than or the same as the other quantity

statements.subject: Mathematics
statements.text: Explore and represent patterns within numbers up to 10, including evens and odds, double facts and how quantities can be distributed equally

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Talk about the lives of the people around them and their roles in society

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Know some similarities and differences between things in the past and now, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Understand the past through settings, characters and events encountered in books read in class and storytelling

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Describe their immediate environment using knowledge from observation, discussion, stories, non-fiction texts and maps

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Know some similarities and differences between different religious and cultural communities in this country, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Explain some similarities and differences between life in this country and life in other countries, drawing on knowledge from stories, non-fiction texts and - when appropriate - maps

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Explore the natural world around them, making observations and drawing pictures of animals and plants

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Know some similarities and differences between the natural world around them and contrasting environments, drawing on their experiences and what has been read in class

statements.subject: Understanding the World
statements.text: Understand some important processes and changes in the natural world around them, including the seasons and changing states of matter

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Safely use and explore a variety of materials, tools and techniques, experimenting with colour, design, texture, form and function

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Share their creations, explaining the process they have used

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Make use of props and materials when role playing characters in narratives and stories

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Invent, adapt and recount narratives and stories with peers and their teacher

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Sing a range of well-known nursery rhymes and songs

statements.subject: Expressive Arts and Design
statements.text: Perform songs, rhymes, poems and stories with others, and - when appropriate - try to move in time with music
